if: tax is payable by a registered person under s.9(3) or s.9(4)
then: that tax IS INPUT TAX in relation to him under s.2(62)(b), and is therefore capable of being credited — subject to s.16, s.17 and s.18 like any other input tax
note: This is the bridge from paying reverse charge to claiming credit for it: without s.2(62)(b) the tax paid under s.9(3) or s.9(4) would not be 'input tax' at all. Capable of being credited is not the same as creditable — s.17(5) still blocks it if the underlying supply is a blocked class. Note also that s.2(62) excludes tax paid under the composition levy. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this provision; later amendments are not held locally.
